title: Restore and Document a Simulated Infrastructure Service
summary: Integrate monitoring, system inspection, troubleshooting, verification, documentation, and escalation in a safe simulation.
objectives: Inspect synthetic telemetry and system records.
Choose only approved low-risk actions in a sandbox scenario.
Document evidence, outcome, uncertainty, and escalation.

vocab.def: Returning a controlled system change to its prior approved state.
A confirmed underlying reason for an observed problem.

sections.heading: The operations challenge
sections.body: A synthetic service is degraded. Monitoring, Linux status, a recent change, and network evidence provide clues, but not every clue is causal.

sections.heading: Deliverable
sections.body: Submit a structured incident record: symptom, evidence, affected system, safe action, result, remaining uncertainty, and escalation.

sections.heading: Safety boundary
sections.body: This is simulation only. Do not connect to production systems, change real equipment, access real credentials, or perform physical electrical, cooling, fiber, or rack work.

practice.prompt: What must be documented before declaring a simulated service restored?
practice.answer: The action, observed outcome, verification evidence, and any remaining uncertainty.

quiz.question: When should a learner escalate?
options: When safety, permission, impact, complexity, or uncertainty requires it
When they want to skip documentation
quiz.answer: When safety, permission, impact, complexity, or uncertainty requires it

lab.objective: Restore and document a simulated service using approved evidence and safe escalation.

reflectionPrompt: What would you communicate to the next authorized person after this simulation?

careerConnection.text: Operations technicians coordinate evidence, safe actions, verification, and handoffs. Completing this project is not professional qualification.
